nodes.label: Competition Rules — Generally Applicable (All Contest Types, Parent Document)
nodes.rationale: Distils the rules common to F3B/F3J/F3K/F5J/F5K/F5L that drive the scoring/running software; child docs reference it where a rule is common and state only their differences.

nodes.label: F3 Soaring — Generally Applicable Rules (Mid-level Parent)
F3B — RC Multi-Task Gliders
nodes.rationale: F3B is the structural outlier: a round is one flight of each of three tasks and each task is normalised separately; there is no single per-group score.

nodes.label: F3J — RC Thermal Duration Gliders
nodes.rationale: The 1 pt/s flight-point rate is not stated in F3J.10; it is the universal reading of F3J and is carried as convention, not as a citation.

F5 Electric Soaring — Generally Applicable Rules (Mid-level Parent)
nodes.rationale: Volume §5.5.1/5.5.2 General/Contest Rules are scoped primarily to F5B (multi-task); the F5 commonalities here are distilled from F5J/F5K/F5L, not lifted from §5.5.1.

Group Score Normalisation (Best Raw = 1000)
nodes.rationale: Universal principle: within each group the best raw result is worth 1000 points and everyone else is scaled to it; where lower is better (speed tasks) the ratio is inverted.

Drop-Worst Rule
Re-Flights — Common Pattern
nodes.rationale: There is no single CIAM re-flight chapter — each class defines its own; five of six classes follow one recognisable pattern but the per-class docs are authoritative on entitlements and exact numbers.

nodes.rationale: The MVP is individual-only and assumes all competitors fly 2.4 GHz spread-spectrum; team rules and frequency-management rules are retained as sport reference but are out of MVP software scope.

nodes.rationale: F3B normalises each of its three tasks separately into a partial score rather than producing one group score — the explicit exception to the universal 1000-point group-score principle.

One Penalty Per Attempt (F3J)
nodes.rationale: For each attempt only one penalty can be given; if a person and in the same attempt an object is touched, the 1000-point penalty applies. Whether limb d) falls inside the same exclusion is a reading, not something the rule states.

nodes.label: F3K Task Catalogue A–N (Per-Task Scored-Time Rules)

F3K No Re-Flight and No Penalty for Free-Flight Mid-Air Collision
nodes.rationale: An exemption no predicate over measurements can express — mid-air collisions in free flight earn no re-flight and no penalty, with the start-phase case as the only exception.

Only Highest Penalty Applies Per Attempt (F3K)
nodes.rationale: Where several safety infractions occur in the same attempt only the highest applies — the rule's own example gives 300, not 400, for a person and an object both inside the safety area.
